clue.text: Pay for enjoyable day

parts.note: something enjoyable is fun

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to pay for a pleasant day out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay for a project is to finance it, a synonym used as a verb.

clue.text: Official list supported by employees

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, held up by it

parts.note: a ship that lists tilts to one side, as anything tips
a firm's employees are its staff

explanation.surface: An official's list of names is backed up by the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'List' looks like a roster but is the verb meaning lean over. A TIPSTAFF is a court officer who attends a judge.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court officer, a kind of official serving judges.

clue.text: Use keys in class

definitions.meaning: to work a keyboard, pressing keys to write
a sort or kind, as in 'not my sort'

explanation.definitionFit: Typing is pressing keys; a type is a category or kind of thing.

clue.text: Part of aircraft also involved in motion

parts.note: a prop is a propeller, part of an aircraft

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of also are mixed

explanation.surface: Part of a plane also features in a debating motion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'motion' looks like movement, but it means a proposal put to a meeting; 'involved' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion put to a meeting is a formal suggestion for debate, a synonym.

clue.text: Worry about old-fashioned look? That's a bit of a bloomer

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to worry is to fret
lo is an archaic word for look or behold

explanation.surface: Fretting over a dated appearance is called something of a gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bloomer' sounds like a blunder, but here it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A floret is one small flower in a composite head, so part of a flowering plant.

clue.text: Guesswork not beginning to reveal criminal activity

indicators.note: the word for guesswork loses its first letter

parts.note: speculation is guesswork

explanation.surface: Guesswork, it turns out, is not how you uncover a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not beginning' removes the first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: Peculation is embezzlement of public money, a form of crime.

clue.text: Boss gets satellite broadcasting location

parts.note: a stud is a boss, a raised knob or ornament
Io is a moon of Jupiter

explanation.surface: A manager takes charge of a satellite broadcasting site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager; it is the ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: A studio is a room from which radio or television programmes are transmitted.

clue.text: Addict trousering sandwiches

indicators.note: the word trousering holds the answer between its outer letters, as bread holds a filling

explanation.surface: A drug addict pockets some sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who takes drugs, so an addict.

clue.text: Get together where students are extremely friendly

parts.note: students attend uni, short for university

indicators.note: the extreme letters, first and last, of the word friendly

explanation.surface: Students at university are urged to unite and be friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: To unify is to bring things together into one whole.

clue.text: Potted meat European found among nettles

indicators.note: one piece is found among, inside, the letters of another

parts.note: nettles as a verb means irritates, riles
a Lett is a Latvian, a European

explanation.surface: Some potted meat is discovered growing among stinging weeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nettles' looks like the plant; it is the verb meaning annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Rillettes is a French spread of shredded pork cooked in fat, a potted meat.

clue.text: Coat may be problem for 18

definitions.meaning: a coat of paint, ... being a water-based wall paint
18 is LAB, a Labrador dog, and canine ... is a dog disease

explanation.definitionFit: Distemper is both a whitewash paint and a viral illness affecting dogs.

clue.text: Source of milk shake judge ignored

indicators.note: the judge's letter is ignored, so left out

parts.note: to judder is to shake violently

explanation.surface: A milkshake with the judge left out of the order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'milk shake' reads as a drink, but 'shake' is fodder; 'ignored' drops J.
explanation.definitionFit: An udder is the gland of a cow or goat that produces milk.

clue.text: Country houses taking last bit of water in river

indicators.note: the river takes in, contains, the letter

parts.note: the Ganges is the great river of India

indicators.note: the final letter of the word water

explanation.surface: Country estates draw the last of the water from a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A grange is a country house with farm buildings.

clue.text: Stop loving and fall asleep

definitions.meaning: to cease liking something or someone

explanation.definitionFit: One can lose one's liking for a food, or doze off: both are idioms with this phrase.

clue.text: Cotton skirts laid up somewhere in Kent

indicators.note: skirts as a verb means goes round the edge of, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: gingham is a checked cotton fabric
someone laid up is ill in bed

explanation.surface: Cotton skirts were stored away somewhere in a southern county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' looks like clothing; it is the verb meaning borders. KENT is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Gillingham is a town in the Medway area of the county of Kent.

clue.text: Wolves, say, with small herbivore in café

indicators.note: the animal goes in the team's letters

parts.note: Wolverhampton Wanderers, known as Wolves, is a football team
roo is a shortened kangaroo, a plant-eater

explanation.surface: A pack of wolves and a small grazing animal share a café.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wolves' suggests the animals, but it is the English football club Wolverhampton Wanderers; 'in' places the kangaroo inside, after the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tearoom is a small restaurant serving tea and light meals, a kind of café.

clue.text: Old lady having half-hearted affair

indicators.note: the doubled middle letter of the word for affair is cut to half, one copy lost

parts.note: an affair is a matter, a business

explanation.surface: An elderly woman is having a lukewarm romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two central Ts. 'Mater' is old public-school slang for mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Mater is Latin and dated British slang for mother, as 'old lady' is.

clue.text: Old king has left on lights etc

parts.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia

explanation.surface: An old king leaves the lights and so on switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lights' suggests lamps; it is the old word for animal lungs, sold as offal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lights are lungs, and offal is the edible internal organs of a carcass, of which they are examples.

clue.text: Cilla Black's little dog

indicators.note: the possessive stands for has, so the singer's name has the letters inside it

explanation.surface: The singer Cilla Black owns a small dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Cilla Black was a British singer and TV presenter. 'Lab' is the short form of Labrador.
explanation.definitionFit: Lab is the clipped form of Labrador, a breed of retriever dog.

clue.text: Butter in trunk found by policeman

indicators.note: found by means placed next to, so the pieces sit together

parts.note: busy is British slang for a police officer or detective
the trunk is the main part of the body

explanation.surface: Butter is discovered in a trunk next to a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter in' reads as a dairy product; it is one who butts in.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody interferes in others' affairs: someone who butts in.

clue.text: Northerners having one night in Quebec?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
nuit is French for night, as spoken in Quebec

explanation.surface: Arctic people spend a single night in a Canadian city.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inuit are indigenous peoples of the Arctic, people of the far north.

clue.text: Posh one leaves fiancée unhusbanded

parts.note: U means upper-class, as in U and non-U

indicators.note: one departs from the word for fiancée, taken out

parts.note: one's intended is one's fiancée
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A posh woman's fiancée walks out, leaving her without a husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unhusbanded' suggests no spouse, but to husband is to tend or conserve resources.
explanation.definitionFit: To husband land is to tend it carefully, so unhusbanded land has been neglected.

clue.text: Like a dandy producing fine work? Fiddlesticks!

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
op is short for opus, a work
pish is an exclamation of contempt, like fiddlesticks

explanation.surface: A dandy is told his fancy work is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: A fop is a vain dandy, so foppish behaviour is dandified.

clue.text: Presenter's first broadcast in braces?

indicators.note: the first letter of the word presenter

parts.note: something broadcast has been aired

explanation.surface: A presenter's first show was broadcast wearing braces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'braces' suggests trouser straps; a brace is a pair, as of game birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A brace means two of something, so items in braces are coupled in twos.

clue.text: Name that's on the door?

definitions.meaning: slang for a person's name or nickname
the knob or lever used to open a door

explanation.definitionFit: A handle is slang for a name, and also the grip you turn to open a door.

clue.text: Kennedy, say, involved in treason

indicators.note: involved means entangled, so the letters of the word are mixed

explanation.surface: A Kennedy is implicated in a plot against the state.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Kennedy and others of the family sat in the US Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: Several Kennedys, such as Edward, served in the US Senate, so the name exemplifies a senator.

clue.text: Dance with cast

definitions.meaning: as in the Highland ..., a lively Scottish dance

explanation.definitionFit: A Highland fling is a Scottish dance; to fling something is to throw it.

clue.text: Iron Duke finally at wit's end — what's in his boots?

parts.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

indicators.note: the final letter of the word Duke
the end, last letter, of the word wit's

explanation.surface: The Iron Duke, at his wits' end, wonders what is inside his boots.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Duke is Wellington, whose name became the rubber boot.
explanation.definitionFit: Feet are what fill one's boots, Wellington boots included.

clue.text: Head teacher ignoring first piece of cake

parts.note: nob is slang for the head

indicators.note: the word for teacher drops its first letter

parts.note: a trainer is a teacher or coach

explanation.surface: A head teacher declines the first slice of cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head teacher' reads as a school head; 'ignoring first' removes T.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for a task so easy it needs no thought.

clue.text: God worries about being ignored

indicators.note: the letter for about is ignored, left out

parts.note: worries are cares
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A god's worries are being disregarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Ares is the Greek god of war.

clue.text: Judge may be going

definitions.meaning: as in the going ..., the usual price

explanation.definitionFit: To rate is to assess; a going rate is the current price.

clue.text: Being looked at, I wept out loud

indicators.note: the words are spoken to give a sound-alike

parts.note: I wept is I bawled, cried loudly

explanation.surface: Being stared at, I cried noisily.
explanation.definitionFit: To be eyeballed is to be stared at closely.

clue.text: 17 not seen as item in programme

indicators.note: not means without, so the letters of the second word are removed

parts.note: the number written in full
taken as written

explanation.surface: Offal goes unnoticed as one course on the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: '17' looks like a cross-reference to 17 across but is just the number spelt out; 'not' removes S...EEN to leave EVENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An event is one item on a programme, as at a sports meeting.
